name: limit_configuration_that_already_exists
why: Two configurations with the same name cannot be made, and SOLIDWORKS says so by returning NULL: no exception, no reason. An operation that did not look at the return value would say «done», and the plan would go on believing it had created the variant -- only to work on the one before, because the active configuration did not change.
_why_it_is_not_a_wrong_argument: The argument is sensible and well written: what is wrong is the STATE of the document. It is the kind of refusal that cannot be caught by reading the call -- it is caught only by looking at how it went.

arguments.name: Left
arguments.details: the second, which must not be born

expect.why: AFTER THE REFUSAL THERE ARE STILL THREE, that is the two of the template plus ours. The error message is written by our code and would say the same sentence even if SOLIDWORKS had created a second «Left»: this line looks at the document, not at the message.

expect._why_true: the refusal did not move anything, so «Left» is still the active one and activating it again is not a move
